- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen next 3–5 days’ forecast by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.30) and price is trending up, model overestimates — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.30) and price is trending down, model underestimates — add 2–5% to forecast to avoid premature reversal.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is deviating > 3σ from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day mean reversion path.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid forecasting > 10% above recent 18-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.50) and volatility is high.
